_about: Public CMS Picker settings, read by `python build\playbook.py publish`. Every answer, each platform's profile and logo, and which platforms are public live in the picker table (admins edit them on the Playbook's CMS Picker tab), separate from the Playbook's own answers. `platforms` here is the display order; other public platforms follow by name. Each row's label finishes "Can you…" in plain words; "term" is the SEO name shown small under it. `quiz` holds the guided quiz's own judgements per platform (the rest of its scoring comes from the answers and profiles). The "cost" section shows each platform's cheapest way to start, as a band from its own pricing page (answers use the cost tags: free, low, mid, high, software, na), with the month it was checked as "asOf".

quiz._about: Find my fit. ease: how easy it is to run without technical skills (0 needs a developer, 3 easiest). look: the design control it suits (template = start from a theme, visual = arrange pages yourself, pixel = every detail). largeCatalogue / smallShop: stores it suits. storeOnly: only for selling, so marked down for anything else. agency: a common choice for designers and agencies; agencyOnly: mostly sold through them. customFrontEnd: built to feed an app or any front end. devControl: built to be coded, so a developer gets full control (picked when "A developer" builds it). domainDocs: the platform's own help page for connecting your own domain (official docs only, checked 2026-10-29; none for self-hosted Drupal or headless), linked from the first steps on a result. kind: for business or work sites, which platforms suit each answer to "Which is closest to what you do?" (from each platform's "good fit" lines: local businesses and services, creative work, startups, B2B companies, lots of content). members: for blogs and publications, the platforms with paid memberships and newsletters built in (from their published profiles).
